exposure: Routine use of in-bag morcellation during laparoscopic hysterectomy
outcome: Spread of cells from unsuspected malignancy
Amount of residual tissue/fluid in the bag
Time associated with the use of the bag
Technical success rate for contained morcellation
Presence of malignant or smooth muscle cells in peritoneal washings
cohort: A consecutive patient cohort of 49 women undergoing laparoscopic hysterectomy primarily for fibroids, adenomyosis, prolapse, or bleeding disorders.
finding: The routine use of in-bag morcellation during laparoscopic hysterectomy achieved a 93.9% technical success rate, with no unsuspected malignancy occurring and all peritoneal washings being negative for malignant or smooth muscle cells.
